mathematical_change.title: Hybrid subcritical ridge plus cross-two tail
mathematical_change.summary: If a residual has both the dependence-safe ridge envelope |phi(t)|<=min(1,(t0/|t|)^beta) and account02/B03's physical cross-two tail |phi(t)|<=min(1,t2/|t|), then the half-Riesz time integral is finite for every beta>0. For beta<1/2 it obeys a mixed-power bound; at beta=1/2 it obeys a logarithmic endpoint bound. This removes the strict theta>q analytic threshold when a cross-two collision tail is present.
mathematical_change.critical_formula: sup_z E|z-R|^{-1/2} <= 2 sqrt(2/pi) sqrt(t0) [2+log_+(t2/t0)] when beta=1/2
mathematical_change.partner_application: For A_m=[1] direct_sum J_m/m direct_sum (-J_m/m) at m=2, Delta=1/4, gamma=1/2,q=1,theta=1, t0=pi e/sqrt(2), t2=2pi, hence ||p_Q||_infinity<8.

failure_lessons_preserved: Do not condition a sum on its conjugate difference and assert a density cap.
Do not infer one uniformly good physical pivot/cross-two certificate from three large eigenvalues.
Do not use the source-refuted worst scalar conditional-density supremum bridge.
Do not claim continuity from the half-Riesz square-pivot density estimate alone.
first_unpaid_implication: Derive from the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis an exhaustive product-preserving structural alternative supplying either direct ridge/cross-rank-three control, a physical square plus the hybrid ridge/cross-two tradeoff, or a grouped/hyperbolic certificate, with dimension-free payment of all local scales.
